title: specular highlights of low roughness surfaces break conservation of energy for big light sources
body: ### Tested versions v4.5.beta.nixpkgs Note: I only tested this in 4.5 but I have noticed oddities that now seem plausible for a very long time. ### System information nixos-unstable, kde wayland, tested in forward + and compatibility ### Issue description Specular reflections of light sources with a size become very bright on surfaces with low roughness the bigger the size is. This makes it difficult to use big light sources in scenes with low roughness objects like glass, polished metal or a tv. As a side-note: big light sources do not reflect at all on surfaces with 0 roughness. I think in practice it is mostly a non-issue, but in my intuition it feels also somewhat wrong. ## Direct comparisons These are identical scenes with the brightness of the lights matched using the wall in the background as a visual aid. Godot: The same scene in blender-eevee (ray tracing disabled) Cycles (reflections of the walls have been disabled) ### Disclaimer I made two somewhat related issues that were both quite confusing and created a heated discussion, so I am starting a fresh issue. I hope that is okay, it feels more productive than trying to salvage the other discussions. ## Scene Comparisons I initially wanted to let this go, but I have issues with lighting in my game that I cannot resolve any other way than writing my own PBR shader. This is not meant to be an apples to apples comparison, but a demonstration of how the issue I explained in abstraction above can mess with the lighting in a scene. For context: I am using point lights to get better shading on the traffic lights and also mimic the reflections that a bright object would cause. And I am getting pretty close to matching the look actually and I find that quite impressive, but some surfaces just look weird. So try to not directly compare godot against cycles here, but look at how the high roughness surfaces look very similar between cycles and godot and observe how the books or the tv kind of fall apart in godot because they look way too bright. ### TV comparison | Godot | Cycles (somewhat unfair comparison) | | -------- | -------- | | | | ### DVD cases comparison | Godot | Cycles (somewhat unfair comparison) | | -------- | -------- | | | | ### Steps to reproduce 1. open the MRP 2. open energy_test.tscn in godot 3. open blender 4. open energy_test.blend 5. enable render preview in blender and make sure eevee is selected as render engine ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [failed to upload, available via google drive (sorry)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OeaQ-IxoSDKLY7uPp1hjy6cZL-DHUVJc/view) The project includes a few more lighting comparisons than what is strictly necessary for this issue. The scene I am using here has a few light sources and a few planes with roughness ranging from 0 to 1 in 0.2 step increments.
